edits.why: Comment points at the maude-v2 brand source. The drawing itself is left alone — see notes.

notes: Every token the canvas and GitPanel.css use is defined in maude-v2 (the old names --accent-muted, --accent-tint and --canvas-* are kept there as aliases), so colours, spacing and type resolve with no token edits.

Locked, left alone: the Changes tab (data-cd-id="changes", data-cd-locked) keeps className="tab". maude-v2 has no .tabbar/.tab rule (its Tabs map to the .seg segmented control), so the Changes/History tabs render as plain buttons after the switch. To move them to .seg, unlock the Changes tab (⇧⌘L) first; the History tab is not changed either, so the two stay consistent.

Callouts: maude-v2's .callout has no info/warn variants and no left accent bar. The 'Anna published 2 changes' nudge (C) and 'Publish didn't go through' (E) lose their tone colour. The classes callout--info / callout--warn are left in place (they are harmless) — decide whether GitPanel.css should draw the tone locally.
Theme: the canvas stays data-theme="dark" (the brief says 'dark studio'). maude-v2 is light-first and its v2 kit canvases use light — decide whether to switch to data-theme="light".

Mark: maude-v2's mark is an azure tile (--accent) with an --accent-fg star, lifted verbatim from assets/logos/mark.svg. The canvas still draws maude's grey bubble with the spark. Not changed here; replacing it is a brand decision.

GitPanel.css is not part of these edits: its header comment still names system/maude and the DS classes it 'lifts' (.panel, .tree-row, .tab, .check). Its rules still apply. ds-check also lists optional alias renames there (--accent-muted → --accent-soft, --accent-tint → --selection, --canvas-* → --x-canvas-*) and some literal font sizes/weights — none of them block the switch.
Before the switch, ds-check --canvas reports the canvas as 'switchable'.
